claims.text: The target material is a high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy.
The initial alloy has a coarse microstructure and an equilibrium phase distribution produced by conventional casting and annealing.
Systematically varying temperature and strain rate under non-equilibrium thermomechanical processing will enhance phase stability.
Systematically varying temperature and strain rate under non-equilibrium thermomechanical processing will refine the microstructure.
The proposed thermomechanical processing will optimize material properties relative to conventional equilibrium processing.
Electron microscopy can characterize microstructural features relevant to property optimization.
In situ XRD can monitor phase and structural evolution during the proposed processing.
The treatment will develop refined grain structures.
The treatment will produce controlled nanoscale precipitates.
Finer microstructural features and particle strengthening can mediate improved mechanical properties.
Refined grains and controlled nanoprecipitates improve thermal properties.
High strain rates and varying temperature induce dynamic phase transformations.
High strain rates and varying temperature enhance atomic diffusion and dislocation activity.
Dynamic phase transformations, atomic diffusion, and dislocation activity cause microstructural refinement and phase stabilization.
The processed samples will have reduced grain size and a more uniform phase distribution than conventionally processed samples.
The processed samples will exhibit improved strength and ductility relative to conventionally processed samples.
Conventional annealing and rolling with lower strain rates and limited temperature variation produce coarser microstructures and less optimized properties.
The effectiveness of the method depends on alloy composition and the selected temperature–strain-rate window.
Inappropriate processing parameters can produce undesirable phases or defects.
Optimal temperatures and strain rates remain undetermined and may differ between materials.
